question.:question/worked-solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\csc x+1\tan x-\cos x) \\  & =(-\csc x\cot x)+1\sec^2 x-(-\sin x) \\  & =1\sec^2 x-\csc x\cot x+\sin x\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real x in a connected component excluding sin(x)=0 and cos(x)=0; sin(x) != 0 and cos(x) != 0.

question.:question/worked-solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x-2\csc x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-2(-\csc xcot⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+2\csc xcot⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{2})}+2\csc (\frac{\pi }{2})\cot (\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }+2\cdot 1\cdot 0 \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Real x in a connected pole-free interval (k*pi,(k+1)*pi), integer k, sin(x) != 0. Require x > 0; intersect with the indicated interval.

We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\csc x-1{x}^{3}+\cos x) \\  & =(-\csc xcot⁡x)-1\cdot 3{x}^{2}+(-\sin x) \\  & =-\csc xcot⁡x-3{x}^{2}-\sin x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-\csc \,(\frac{\pi }{4})\cot \,(\frac{\pi }{4})-3{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}-\sin \,(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot 1-3\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\sqrt{2}-\frac{3}{16}{\pi }^{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{3}{16}{\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
